arch_decisions.decision: Create NEW file backend/internal/repository/postgres_dml_table_check.go (package repository) exporting func DMLCorrectSQLTargetTableWarning(qType, correctSQL, targetTable string) string. Return '' when qType != 'DML' or targetTable is empty. arch_decisions.decision: Every new column defaults off/empty; previewSchema/useDecoy default to ''/false; there is NO backfill, NO re-capture, NO re-score. A question with dual_schema=false and an owner with no preview schema must preview and grade EXACTLY as before this feature. The validator must diff a non-dual question's preview rows, verdict, score, and feedback against pre-feature behavior and require equality. Global constraint enforced by validator/regression-tester. The dual-without-decoy fallback (spec 6.1) is part of this guarantee: a question with dual_schema=true whose owner has no decoy schema previews AND grades on B, i.e. it is behaviourally identical to a single-schema question. The condition is reported to the LECTURER only (backend dual_schema_warning on save + server-side log; frontend inline validation) and is never surfaced to the student and never blocks a student action.
arch_decisions.rationale: The feature is strictly opt-in; the load-bearing safety property is that untouched questions are indistinguishable from today.

arch_decisions.req: GAP 1 (CRITICAL, found by merge-check): spec s7.1 wrongly asserts 'Submit returns no rows today'. ValidationResult.ValidationDetails (models/submission.go:18) IS populated with the rows produced by executing the STUDENT's SQL against grading schema B (postgres_evaluation.go evaluateQuery:107-111 / evaluateDML:194-198), is returned to the student (practice_controller.go:132, quiz_controller.go:278), is persisted (postgres_practice.go:628, postgres_results.go:36), is re-served on student read paths (postgres_practice.go:639, postgres_results.go:12/:54) and is rendered as row tables by frontend/src/components/StudentResults.vue:318-332. On a dual question a student submits 'SELECT * FROM <table>' and gets schema B's real rows back, defeating the whole feature. Close every B-derived channel on the student-facing submit/results/question payloads, dual-only, without changing grading or the preview.
arch_decisions.decision: (a) SINGLE FAIL-SAFE CHOKE POINT in the service layer. In backend/internal/services/validation_service.go, change ValidationService.Validate (currently :27) to use NAMED return values `(result models.ValidationResult, err error)` and install, as its FIRST statement, a deferred scrub gated on `question.DualSchema`. Because a deferred func runs AFTER the return expression is evaluated, `s.decideStatus(result, studentData, result.Columns, question)` (:54) has already consumed ValidationDetails and Columns for grading before the scrub runs - grading semantics are therefore provably unchanged. The scrub sets `result.ValidationDetails = nil` and `result.Columns = nil`, and additionally, when `result.Status == "syntax_error"`, replaces result.Feedback with a package-level constant (suggested name dualExecErrorFeedback = "Your SQL could not be executed against the grading dataset. Use Test Run to check your statement.") after log.Printf-ing the original feedback together with studentID and question.ID server-side so the lecturer/ops can still diagnose A/B structure drift. Status, IsCorrect, Score and the non-error Feedback strings are left untouched (they are the verdict, which the student is entitled to). The defer is total over EVERY current and future return path of Validate, including the empty-SQL early return (:29-35) and the `result.Status == "error"` early return (:42-47), and cannot be forgotten by a later edit - that is why it is preferred over an inline clear before the final return. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE - stripping on each student-facing read path: it needs edits at five-plus sites (practice_controller.go:132, quiz_controller.go:278, ListPracticeAttempts postgres_practice.go:639, GetStudentExamResults postgres_results.go:54, plus every future read path), each requiring a new JOIN onto practice_questions.dual_schema / questions.dual_schema on hot read queries, and it would still leave B's rows at rest in the database. One missed site is a total leak. The service choke point is fail-closed and touches one file. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE - scrubbing in the repository (postgres_evaluation.go): impossible, the repository MUST return the rows because decideStatus/decideDMLStatus in the service are the graders. (b) PERSISTENCE - dual questions persist NO validation_details, and this needs ZERO repository/SQL work. Because the scrub happens inside Validate, the controllers build models.PracticeAttempt (practice_controller.go:114-120) and models.Submission (quiz_controller.go:263-271) from an already-nil field, so both INSERTs write SQL NULL into the nullable `validation_details JSONB` column (postgres_schema.go:991 and :1033). Consequences, all accepted: student read-backs return JSON null and StudentResults.vue:318 already guards with `v-if="q.submission && q.submission.validation_details"`, so the details row simply does not render - NO frontend change. Lecturer diagnostics via GetSubmissionsByExamID (lecturer_controller.go:428) show validation_details: null for dual submissions; acceptable because sql_text, is_correct and score are still persisted and the lecturer owns schema B and can reproduce the rows by replaying the persisted sql_text through the lecturer preview on B. EXPORT PATHS NEED NO CHANGE: postgres_export.go:55 and :85 already wrap the column in COALESCE(...::text, ''), so dual rows export an empty cell with the CSV header and column count unchanged (submission_export.go:62, :89). Implementors MUST NOT modify postgres_export.go, submission_export.go, postgres_results.go, postgres_practice.go or postgres_evaluation.go under this decision. (c) PREVIEW IS ALREADY CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE 'FIXED'. ValidationService.ValidatePreview (:60) and repository evaluateQueryPreview/evaluateDMLPreview return decoy schema A's rows DELIBERATELY - that is the feature (spec s6). The scrub is scoped to Validate ONLY; no implementor may add row-clearing to any *Preview* function or to the preview response builders (practice_controller.go:201-208, quiz_controller.go PreviewAnswer). The dual-without-decoy fallback (spec 6.1) still previews on B by design; that is the already-accepted, logged trade-off and is out of scope here. (d) NO BACKFILL. The dual_schema columns were added in this same pipeline run as `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS ... BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false` with no UPDATE, so every historical row in app.submissions and app.practice_attempts belongs to a non-dual question and contains no B-secret. No migration, no data fix-up, no re-score, no audit script. (e) SWEEP OF OTHER B-DERIVED FIELDS. (e1) ValidationResult.Columns is `json:"-"` so it never serializes, but nil it anyway for defence in depth. (e2) ValidationResult.Feedback on syntax_error carries fmt.Sprintf("SQL Error: %v", err) from the student's SQL executed against B (postgres_evaluation.go:114 and :201). pgconn.PgError.Error() (vendor/github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgconn/errors.go:53-55) emits only Severity+Message+SQLSTATE, so DETAIL/HINT lines with literal key values are NOT included - but Message is still a data-dependent oracle over B (a crafted expression such as a division-by-zero guarded by a subquery predicate turns each submit into an arbitrary yes/no question about B's data), so it is genericised for dual per (a). (e3) Dual DML mismatch Feedback is ALREADY generic via ARCH-007 (validation_service.go:152-159) - verify it still is, no new work. (e4) Status/IsCorrect/Score are the verdict; inherent to grading, unchanged. (e5) NEW WORK - Question.CaptureError (models/submission.go:61) and Question.ExpectedRowsAffected (:60), and PracticeQuestion.CaptureError (models/practice.go:67) and .ExpectedRowsAffected (:72), ARE B-derived (the Postgres error text from running the LECTURER's correct_sql on B, and the rows-affected count of the lecturer's correct DML on B - a direct numeric answer hint) and are currently shipped to students because the existing strip loops only clear CorrectSQL/ExpectedResult/ExpectedColumns. Extend the THREE existing strip sites, dual-only, using the DualSchema flag which is already loaded on all three paths: practice_controller.go ListForStudent loop at :43-47, practice_controller.go GetForStudent at :66-68, and quiz_controller.go GetExamQuestions loop at :145-151 (which already branches on questions[i].DualSchema). In each, when the question is dual, set CaptureError = "" and ExpectedRowsAffected = nil; both fields carry omitempty so the keys vanish from the JSON entirely. (e6) Question.CurriculumSchema is omitempty, is populated only by GetQuestion (not by GetQuestionsByExamID, postgres_questions.go:326), and is a schema NAME not data - left alone here; see the residual-risk note about schema-qualified access. (e7) SSE payloads (buildExamStatusEvent) carry exam status only, no submission data - no change. (e8) TargetTable, StrictMode and ExpectedResultStatus are structural/metadata and identical between A and B by spec s2 decision 1 - no change. BACK-COMPAT: every behaviour above is gated on q.DualSchema. For dual_schema=false the submit response bytes, the persisted rows, the read-back payloads and the export CSVs are byte-identical to today, INCLUDING still returning and storing validation_details. PARALLELISM NOTE: the service change (validation_service.go) and the controller change (practice_controller.go + quiz_controller.go) are behaviourally independent and file-disjoint, so they may be split into two parallel groups. Keep practice_controller.go and quiz_controller.go in the SAME group - they are the same Go package and each implementor runs `go build ./...`.
arch_decisions.rationale: The merge-check finding is real and the spec assertion it contradicts is factually wrong, so no existing TODO covers it. A defer in ValidationService.Validate is the only point through which BOTH student submit paths (practice_controller.go:111 and quiz_controller.go:240 are the only two callers of Validate in the whole codebase, vendor excluded) pass, and it sits AFTER grading but BEFORE the controllers construct the persisted rows - so one edit closes the response leak, the at-rest leak and every present and future read-back leak simultaneously, while grading provably still sees the data it needs. Read-path stripping was rejected because it is five-plus edits, adds JOINs to hot queries, still stores B's rows on disk, and fails open if any site is missed. Not persisting is preferable to persist-then-strip because the lecturer's diagnostic loss is small (sql_text is retained and the lecturer can replay it on B, which they own) while the security gain is that B's rows never touch a student-readable table at all. The capture_error / expected_rows_affected finding is a second, independent leak on the question payload that the same sweep uncovered: expected_rows_affected literally tells the student how many rows the correct answer touches on B, which is precisely the brute-force hint this feature exists to remove.

A3 (unit, services): for identical executor output, Status, IsCorrect and Score are EQUAL between the DualSchema=true and DualSchema=false runs - proving the scrub happens strictly after decideStatus and grading semantics did not change.

arch_decisions.req: GAP 2 (MEDIUM, found by merge-check): hard-delete paths leak orphaned Postgres schemas forever. ArchiveExamination drops sandbox_exam_<id>_preview (postgres_exams.go:128-138, ARCH-002) but DeleteExamination (postgres_exams.go:294) drops neither curriculum_exam_<id>_preview nor sandbox_exam_<id>_preview, and DeletePracticeCategory (postgres_practice.go:233) never drops practice_cat_<id>_preview. Reclaim decoy schema A on hard delete, mirroring each function's existing non-preview drop.
arch_decisions.decision: (1) DeleteExamination, backend/internal/repository/postgres_exams.go:294. Inside the existing WithTransaction closure, add a new step '5c. Decoy preview schemas (dual-schema grading)' immediately after the existing step 5b curriculum drop (ends :353) and before step 6 (:356). Drop BOTH ExamPreviewCurriculumSchemaName(id) and ExamPreviewSandboxName(id) (both defined in postgres_preview_schema.go:31 and :38) UNCONDITIONALLY by canonical name, each sanitized with pgx.Identifier{name}.Sanitize() and executed as `DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS %s CASCADE`. A failure of either drop is logged with fmt.Printf("Warning: failed to drop ... during delete: %v\n", ...) and execution CONTINUES - exactly matching the warn-and-continue treatment this same function already gives the real sandbox (:337-339) and the real curriculum (:350-352). Unconditional-by-name, NOT gated on reading examinations.preview_curriculum_schema: this matches the precedent ARCH-002 already set in ArchiveExamination (:128-138) and additionally reclaims a schema left behind by a failed or partial decoy import that never stamped the column. IF EXISTS makes it a no-op when the schema is absent. The `!= 'public'` guard used for curriculum_schema (:348) is unnecessary and must NOT be copied: both names are derived from the exam id and can never be 'public'. Take NO advisory lock here - this function takes none for its real sandbox or curriculum drops either, and adding one only for the decoy would be inconsistent and is not required to close the leak (recorded as accepted residual risk). Position inside the transaction is what matters; relative order versus the DELETE FROM app.examinations at :361 is immaterial because both names come from `id`. (2) DeletePracticeCategory, backend/internal/repository/postgres_practice.go:233. Inside the existing WithTransaction closure, add a preview block AFTER the existing real-schema block (:265-276), for PracticeCategoryPreviewSchemaName(id) (postgres_preview_schema.go:25): first acquireSchemaRebuildLockTx(ctx, tx, previewSchema) - the SAME lock discipline ARCH-013 applies to the real schema, and it is load-bearing here because evaluateDMLPreview takes the shared eval lock on the preview schema (postgres_evaluation.go:321), so without it an in-flight dual DML preview could be dropped out from under a student - then `DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS %s CASCADE` on the pgx.Identifier-sanitized name. If EITHER the lock acquisition OR the drop fails, log fmt.Printf("Warning: ...") and CONTINUE; do NOT `return err`. This deliberately DIFFERS from the real-schema block directly above it, which returns err and aborts: the real schema holds the graded dataset so failing to drop it is a correctness problem worth aborting on, whereas the decoy is display-only and aborting an entire category delete over it would be worse than leaking one schema - and this matches the ArchiveExamination preview-drop precedent at postgres_exams.go:136-138. Unconditional by canonical name: do NOT gate on practice_categories.preview_schema_name and do NOT modify the SELECT at :236-237, for the same partial-import reason as (1). The block sits inside the closure so it runs on both the force and non-force paths, and - critically - it is still behind the ErrCategoryProtected / ErrCategoryHasQuestions guards at :243-254, so a blocked delete drops nothing. LOCK ORDERING CONVENTION established here: when a single transaction takes both a real-schema and a preview-schema rebuild lock, take the REAL schema lock first, then the PREVIEW schema lock. No existing code path takes both, so there is no deadlock today; this ordering is the convention future code must follow. (3) NO CHANGE to ArchiveExamination. It already drops sandbox_exam_<id>_preview (ARCH-002). It intentionally does NOT drop curriculum_exam_<id>_preview: archive does not drop the real curriculum_schema either, so the decoy curriculum must survive an archive for a later un-archive or reuse. Only hard delete reclaims it. An implementor must not 'harmonise' these. SCOPE GUARD: this decision touches only postgres_exams.go and postgres_practice.go plus one new test file. postgres_preview_schema.go, postgres_schema.go and postgres_rebuild_lock.go are read-only for it - the naming helpers and the lock helper already exist and are used as-is.
arch_decisions.rationale: Both leaks are the same class of bug: a hard-delete path was extended for the real schema when per-owner schemas were introduced, but the decoy schema added by this feature was only wired into the archive path. An orphaned Postgres schema is never garbage-collected, holds a full copy of a dataset, and its canonical name is derived from an id that will be reused by nothing - so the leak is permanent and unbounded in a long-lived deployment. Dropping unconditionally by canonical name rather than by the stamped column makes the cleanup robust to partial imports, which is exactly the state in which an orphan is most likely to exist. Warn-and-continue for the decoy is right because the decoy is display-only: a delete that half-succeeds and then aborts leaves the operator worse off than one that completes and logs a reclaimable schema. Taking the rebuild lock in the practice path (but not the exam path) is not an inconsistency but a faithful mirror of what each function already does for its own schemas.

arch_decisions.req: GAP 3 (CRITICAL, confirmed): the dual-schema preview hides grading schema B only cosmetically. Student SQL is never checked for schema qualification (validateNoSchemaQualifiedNames is import-only) and exam_student_readonly / exam_student hold USAGE+SELECT on EVERY real curriculum and category schema (postgres_schema.go:826-828, 888-890, 1281-1283, 1306-1308). So inside a dual preview (search_path = decoy A, role exam_student_readonly) a student can run `SELECT * FROM curriculum_exam_7.employees` or `SELECT * FROM practice_cat_3.employees` and read B's rows in full, unlimited, with no submission recorded, after enumerating names from pg_namespace. USER DECISION (locked): fix at the engine with preview-only database roles that hold USAGE on the decoy schema only; explicitly NOT by parsing/blocklisting student SQL (untrustworthy against quoting, comments, CTEs, dynamic constructs).
arch_decisions.decision:
TWO new NOLOGIN Postgres roles, used ONLY when a preview resolves to a decoy schema.

(1) ROLE IDENTITY. `exam_student_preview_readonly` (SELECT-only; used by the dual QUERY preview) and `exam_student_preview` (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; used by the dual DML preview, which really does write into the decoy sandbox inside a SAVEPOINT). Two roles, not one: a single writable role would let a QUERY preview run a data-modifying CTE against the shared decoy, which today's exam_student_readonly rejects at the engine — that property must be preserved. Names mirror the existing exam_student / exam_student_readonly pair (postgres_schema.go:29-49). Declare package constants in backend/internal/repository/postgres_preview_schema.go: `const rolePreviewStudent = "exam_student_preview"` and `const rolePreviewStudentReadonly = "exam_student_preview_readonly"`.

(2) ROLE CREATION (idempotent, boot-only). In postgres_schema.go `CreateRestrictedUser` (:29-49) append to the existing `queries` slice, after the exam_student_readonly block, using the SAME DO-block catalog-check pattern already in the file (CREATE ROLE ... IF NOT EXISTS is not valid Postgres):
  - "DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_catalog.pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'exam_student_preview') THEN CREATE ROLE exam_student_preview NOLOGIN NOINHERIT; END IF; END $$"
  - "REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA public FROM exam_student_preview"
  - "DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_catalog.pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'exam_student_preview_readonly') THEN CREATE ROLE exam_student_preview_readonly NOLOGIN NOINHERIT; END IF; END $$"
  - "REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA public FROM exam_student_preview_readonly"
Deliberately ABSENT (the asymmetry vs the two existing roles): no GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public, no GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public, no ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES in public, and no role membership in exam_student/exam_student_readonly. CreateRestrictedUser is already called at boot (cmd/main.go:57) and by internal/testsupport/db.go:68 and internal/repository openTestRepo (postgres_password_events_test.go:41), so `docker compose down && up` self-heals with NO new call site, NO migration file and NO manual DBA step. The app connects as the `postgres` superuser (.env DATABASE_URL), so SET LOCAL ROLE to the new roles needs no membership grant — exactly as today's exam_student does.

(3) GRANT TOPOLOGY (asymmetric on purpose). New helper in postgres_preview_schema.go:
  func (r *PostgresRepository) grantPreviewSchemaPermissions(ctx context.Context, schema string, allowDML bool) error
Built like the existing grant helpers (pgx.Identifier{schema}.Sanitize(), r.pool.Exec per statement, fmt.Errorf wrap):
  a. GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA s TO exam_student_preview_readonly
  b. GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA s TO exam_student_preview_readonly
  c. ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA s GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO exam_student_preview_readonly
  d. if allowDML: GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA s TO exam_student_preview; GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA s TO exam_student_preview; ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA s GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLES TO exam_student_preview
  e. asymmetry + self-heal for decoys provisioned by the pre-ARCH-020 code: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA s REVOKE ALL ON TABLES FROM exam_student, exam_student_readonly; REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA s FROM exam_student, exam_student_readonly; REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA s FROM exam_student, exam_student_readonly.
No sequence grants — deliberate parity with GrantSchemaPermissions (postgres_schema.go:216-230), which grants tables only.
CALL SITES (replace the current grant blocks entirely; decoys must NOT keep the same posture as real schemas):
  - ensureCategoryPreviewSchema (postgres_preview_schema.go:49-69): delete the r.GrantSchemaPermissions call (:54) and the whole readonlyQueries block (:57-67); call grantPreviewSchemaPermissions(ctx, schema, true) — practice runs BOTH its QUERY and its DML preview against this one decoy schema, so it needs the writable role too.
  - ensureExamPreviewCurriculumSchema (:78-95): replace the readonlyQueries block with grantPreviewSchemaPermissions(ctx, schema, false) — exam QUERY previews only; exam DML previews use the preview sandbox.
  - InitializeExamPreviewSandbox (:349-372): replace r.GrantSchemaPermissions(ctx, schema) (:368) with grantPreviewSchemaPermissions(ctx, schema, true), keeping it BEFORE ensureTablesInSchema so ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES covers the cloned tables.
EXPLICITLY UNTOUCHED: GrantSchemaPermissions, ensureCategorySchema, ensureExamCurriculumSchema and every real-schema grant site (postgres_schema.go:782, 820-828, 882-890, 1276-1283, 1294-1308) keep today's exam_student / exam_student_readonly grants byte-for-byte. HARD INVARIANT: neither new role may ever be granted USAGE on public, app, sandbox_practice, practice_cat_<id>, curriculum_exam_<id> or sandbox_exam_<id>.

(4) BOOT RECONCILIATION (so already-imported decoys self-heal). New func in postgres_preview_schema.go:
  func (r *PostgresRepository) reconcilePreviewSchemaGrants(ctx context.Context) error
Enumerate `SELECT nspname FROM pg_catalog.pg_namespace WHERE nspname LIKE 'practice\_cat\_%\_preview' OR nspname LIKE 'curriculum\_exam\_%\_preview' OR nspname LIKE 'sandbox\_exam\_%\_preview'` and call grantPreviewSchemaPermissions for each, with allowDML = (name is practice_cat_*_preview OR sandbox_exam_*_preview), false for curriculum_exam_*_preview. Per-schema failures are log.Printf'd and skipped (never fatal); only a failure of the enumeration query itself is returned. Call it as the LAST statement of CreateRestrictedUser (after the role loop), so it runs at boot and in every test bootstrap without a new call site. Without this, a decoy imported by the already-merged ARCH-002 code would have no grants for the new roles and its dual preview would fail with permission denied.

(5) RUNTIME ROLE SELECTION (postgres_evaluation.go). In EvaluatePreview (:225) compute `useDecoy := previewSchema != ""` BEFORE the existing empty-string fallbacks; that flag is the single, exact rule — previewSchema is non-empty only when a controller resolved a real decoy (practice_controller.go:176-189, quiz_controller.go:331-362). Then:
  - QUERY branch: role := "exam_student_readonly"; if useDecoy { role = rolePreviewStudentReadonly }; pass role to evaluateQueryPreview.
  - DML branch: role := "exam_student"; if useDecoy { role = rolePreviewStudent }; pass role to evaluateDMLPreview.
Add a trailing `role string` parameter to evaluateQueryPreview (:240) and evaluateDMLPreview (:296); replace the hardcoded `SET LOCAL ROLE exam_student_readonly` (:264) and `SET LOCAL ROLE exam_student` (:333) with fmt.Sprintf("SET LOCAL ROLE %s", pgx.Identifier{role}.Sanitize()). Nothing else in those functions changes — same search_path, same savepoint, same RESET ROLE / ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT ordering, same 30 s timeout, same 200-row cap. Because the non-decoy defaults are today's literals, a non-dual preview issues byte-identical SQL. Evaluate / querySchemaFor / evaluateQuery / evaluateDML (:25-217) — the WHOLE grading path — are not touched at all, so grading keeps full access to B, which is correct: grading never returns B's rows to the student (ARCH-018 scrubs the payload).

(6) NO-DECOY FALLBACK (spec 6.1) — KEEP TODAY'S ROLE. When dual_schema=true but the owner has no decoy, previewSchema resolves to "", so useDecoy is false and the preview runs on B under exam_student_readonly / exam_student exactly as today. This is deliberate: (a) in that state the preview IS B, so a schema-qualified read of B discloses nothing the preview does not already show — no incremental leak; (b) using the restricted role there would fail with permission denied on B, converting a lecturer misconfiguration into a hard-broken student preview, which the locked spec 6.1 forbids ("the student is never blocked"). The existing dual_schema_warning + server-side fallback log remain the mitigation.

(7) pg_catalog / information_schema — NO CHANGE, accepted. Schema NAMES stay enumerable (pg_namespace is world-readable and the decoy names are deterministic anyway), while CONTENTS are denied by the missing USAGE. Revoking catalog visibility is database-global, breaks pgx/psql type resolution, and buys only obscurity; the security boundary is USAGE, not secrecy of names. One documented consequence of the same reasoning: on schema `public` the PUBLIC pseudo-role grants USAGE by default and REVOKE ... FROM <role> cannot remove it, so the preview roles may retain USAGE on public — harmless because table-level SELECT in public is never granted to them (so `SELECT * FROM public.<t>` still fails), and we deliberately do NOT run a database-wide `REVOKE ... FROM PUBLIC`.

(8) BLAST RADIUS. Four files, all disjoint from the in-flight TODO-021/022/023 scopes. No model, controller, service, route, frontend or migration change. No behavior change for non-dual questions, grading, capture, imports or the lecturer preview (PreviewPracticeCorrectSQL / lecturer preview run as the app superuser with no SET ROLE and are unaffected, including their schema="preview" decoy mode).
arch_decisions.rationale:
Engine-enforced authorization is the only trustworthy boundary here: any SQL-text denylist (the import-time validateNoSchemaQualifiedNames approach) can be evaded with quoted identifiers, comments, CTEs, set-returning functions or search_path tricks, and it would have to be maintained forever. A role that simply lacks USAGE on B makes the leak a Postgres error, no matter how the student spells the query. Two roles rather than one preserve the existing read-only guarantee for QUERY previews (no write-CTE side effects on the shared decoy). Grants live on the decoy provisioning paths because those are the only places a decoy schema comes into existence, plus one boot-time reconciliation so decoys created by the already-merged ARCH-002 code pick up the new posture without a DBA step. Reusing CreateRestrictedUser for role creation costs zero new call sites and is already exercised by main.go, testsupport and openTestRepo. Keeping today's role on the no-decoy fallback trades a leak that discloses nothing new for a preview that keeps working, which is what spec 6.1 locked in.

RESIDUAL RISK ACCEPTED, NOT FIXED HERE (flag to the user, candidate GAP 4): hiding is per-OWNER, not per-question. If an exam/category contains BOTH a dual and a non-dual question, the student can open the NON-dual question's preview — which legitimately runs on B under exam_student_readonly — and from there read the whole of B, including the tables behind the dual question. ARCH-020 closes the leak inside dual previews only. Closing this would require routing every preview for a decoyed owner to the decoy (an owner-level toggle), which contradicts the locked per-question design and ARCH-016's back-compat guarantee. Interim mitigation is lecturer guidance: in a dual-schema owner, make ALL questions dual. Two smaller accepted risks: (i) a student query that calls a function or reads a table living in `public` will now fail under the preview roles (no SELECT there) — acceptable because decoy previews are meant to be self-contained, and structure parity is already warned on import; (ii) stale exam_student grants on pre-existing decoys are cleaned by the boot reconciliation, but only for schemas matching the three canonical name patterns.

arch_decisions.req: CRITICAL (supersedes/completes ARCH-020, which the validator correctly failed as insufficient): student-submitted DML is executed as a MULTI-STATEMENT simple-protocol query, so a student can escape the restricted role entirely. Verified chain: (a) .env sets DB_USER=postgres, so the app connects as a SUPERUSER; (b) student DML runs via argument-less tx.Exec(ctx, studentSQL) at backend/internal/repository/postgres_evaluation.go:168 (graded evaluateDML) and :366 (evaluateDMLPreview); (c) vendored pgx v5.9.2 conn.go:515 reads verbatim '// Always use simple protocol when there are no arguments.' followed by 'if len(arguments) == 0 { mode = QueryExecModeSimpleProtocol }', and that override runs AFTER any QueryExecMode passed in args has been consumed, so tx.Exec(ctx, sql, pgx.QueryExecModeExec) is a no-op; (d) simple protocol allows many statements per query string, so 'RESET ROLE; <anything>' fully defeats SET LOCAL ROLE. Re-confirmed by the architect against a live postgres:15-alpine: with SET LOCAL ROLE exam_student, tx.Exec(ctx, "RESET ROLE; INSERT INTO t SELECT 0 FROM bee.secret") returned CommandTag 'INSERT 0 1' even though the same statement WITHOUT the 'RESET ROLE; ' prefix returns 'permission denied for schema bee (SQLSTATE 42501)'. Impact: on ANY DML question (dual or not, practice or exam) a student submits 'RESET ROLE; INSERT INTO <target_table> SELECT email, password_hash FROM app.system_users;' and reads the harvested rows back out of the post-image capture (postgres_evaluation.go:172 graded / :376 preview). Reads are NOT undone by the rollback. This PREDATES the dual-schema feature and defeats the entire premise of ARCH-018/ARCH-019/ARCH-020. Fix: make the ENGINE guarantee that student SQL is exactly one statement, at both DML sites, without disturbing lecturer schema imports (which legitimately execute whole uploaded .sql files as one multi-statement tx.Exec at postgres_schema.go:415, postgres_schema.go:504, postgres_preview_schema.go:272, postgres_preview_schema.go:379) and without changing grading semantics.
arch_decisions.decision:
MECHANISM (chosen): execute student SQL through the PostgreSQL EXTENDED QUERY PROTOCOL via tx.Conn().PgConn().ExecParams(...). Postgres's Parse message accepts at most one command per statement string (exec_parse_message() in postgres.c raises 'cannot insert multiple commands into a prepared statement', SQLSTATE 42601), so single-statement-ness is enforced by the SERVER, not by any text inspection in Go.

(0) REJECTED ALTERNATIVES, each disproven empirically by the architect against a live postgres:15-alpine before this entry was written.
  - tx.Exec(ctx, sql, pgx.QueryExecModeExec): DEAD, see req (c).
  - Setting DefaultQueryExecMode on the pool: DEAD FOR Exec for exactly the same reason. Measured: with cfg.ConnConfig.DefaultQueryExecMode pinned to QueryExecModeCacheStatement, tx.Exec(ctx, "CREATE TABLE z1(a int); CREATE TABLE z2(b int); INSERT INTO z1 VALUES(1);") still SUCCEEDS. So the concern recorded in the brief is inverted: changing the default mode does not break the four schema-import sites, but it also does not fix the vulnerability. It is a no-op here, not a trade-off.
  - tx.Prepare(ctx, name, studentSQL) then execute: works only by accident of pgx's lookup order (the c.preparedStatements[sql] short-circuit at conn.go:530 happens to precede the mode switch), and it leaves a NAMED server-side prepared statement on a POOLED connection whose PREPARE is rolled back with the transaction while pgx's client-side map is not - the classic pgx 'prepared statement does not exist' footgun on the next checkout of that connection. REJECTED as fragile.
  - SQL text parsing / statement splitting / blocklisting 'RESET ROLE': REJECTED by user decision and independently unsound (semicolons inside strings, comments and dollar-quoting).

(1) NEW FILE backend/internal/repository/postgres_student_exec.go - the single chokepoint for executing UNTRUSTED (student) SQL.
  - var errMultipleStatements = errors.New("student SQL contained more than one statement") (package-private sentinel).
  - const MultiStatementFeedback = "Only one SQL statement can be submitted for this question. Please remove the extra statement(s) and submit a single statement." EXPORTED, because services/validation_service.go must be able to recognise it by exact equality (see (5)). It names no schema, no table, no role, no SQLSTATE and no internal identifier.
  - func execStudentStatement(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, sql string) (pgconn.CommandTag, error): calls rr := tx.Conn().PgConn().ExecParams(ctx, sql, nil, nil, nil, nil) then tag, err := rr.Close(). rr.Close() MUST be called exactly once and unconditionally on every path (the pgconn contract: the ResultReader must be closed before the PgConn is usable again); it both drains any rows (so 'INSERT ... RETURNING' works) and yields the CommandTag. RETURN CONTRACT IS IDENTICAL TO tx.Exec: (pgconn.CommandTag, error). tag.RowsAffected() therefore keeps working verbatim - measured: 'INSERT INTO t VALUES (4) RETURNING id' -> tag 'INSERT 0 1', RowsAffected()==1; 'SELECT * FROM t' -> tag 'SELECT n'. Any future RowsAffected-based guard (e.g. ARCH-008's 0-row vacuity check) is a drop-in.
  - Error classification, DISPLAY-ONLY: if errors.As(err, &pgErr) && pgErr.Code == "42601" && pgErr.Routine == "exec_parse_message", return the tag and fmt.Errorf("%w", errMultipleStatements); otherwise return err unchanged. pgErr.Routine is the C function name and is NEVER localised, so this is locale-independent - measured discriminator: multi-statement -> Code 42601 / Routine 'exec_parse_message'; ordinary syntax errors -> Code 42601 / Routine 'scanner_yyerror'; missing relation -> 42P01 / 'parserOpenTable'. CRITICAL PROPERTY, state it in the doc comment: this classification only chooses WHICH SENTENCE THE STUDENT SEES. Security does not depend on it. If it ever misclassifies, the statement is still rejected by the server and the student merely sees the raw SQL error. That is why this is not the text-matching the user rejected: nothing about whether the SQL runs is decided in Go.
  - func studentSQLErrorFeedback(err error) string: returns MultiStatementFeedback when errors.Is(err, errMultipleStatements), else fmt.Sprintf("SQL Error: %v", err) - byte-identical to today's two call sites for every other error.
  - File-header doc comment must record: WHY this exists (pgx conn.go:515), that any new execution of student-supplied SQL MUST go through this helper, and that tx.Exec must never be used for student SQL again.

(2) CALL SITE A - backend/internal/repository/postgres_evaluation.go, evaluateDML, line 168. Replace 'if _, execErr := tx.Exec(ctx, studentSQL); execErr != nil' with 'if _, execErr := execStudentStatement(ctx, tx, studentSQL); execErr != nil'. The whole surrounding block is otherwise unchanged: the savepoint (:152), SET LOCAL search_path (:157), SET LOCAL ROLE exam_student (:160) and the post-image capture 'SELECT * FROM <target>' (:172) all stay exactly as they are - measured: session state set by tx.Exec (search_path, SET LOCAL ROLE) applies to ExecParams on the same connection, so behaviour for a legitimate single statement is unchanged. At :201 change 'result.Feedback = fmt.Sprintf("SQL Error: %v", studentErr)' to 'result.Feedback = studentSQLErrorFeedback(studentErr)'.
  MANDATORY ADJACENT FIX AT THE SAME SITE (found while verifying this design; without it the required negative test cannot pass): today, when the student's statement errors, the transaction is left in the aborted state (SQLSTATE 25P02) and the very next statement, 'RESET ROLE' at :185, FAILS - measured 'ERROR: current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block (25P02)' - whereupon evaluateDML returns a hard error, ValidationService.Validate propagates it, and quiz_controller.go:267 / practice_controller.go:142 answer HTTP 500 with the raw err.Error() in the body. So TODAY EVERY FAILED STUDENT DML SUBMISSION IS A 500 THAT LEAKS INTERNAL TEXT, and after this change a 'RESET ROLE; ...' attempt would take that same path. FIX: swap the order of the two statements at :185-:192 so 'ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT student_eval' runs FIRST and 'RESET ROLE' second. Measured: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT succeeds even in the aborted state and by itself restores current_user to the app role (the savepoint at :152 is taken BEFORE the SET LOCAL ROLE at :160), so the subsequent RESET ROLE is belt-and-braces and cannot fail. KEEP both error checks fatal exactly as they are today (rollback the whole tx and return the error) - only the ORDER changes. Do not otherwise restructure evaluateDML.

(3) CALL SITE B - backend/internal/repository/postgres_evaluation.go, evaluateDMLPreview, line 366. Same substitution: 'if _, execErr := execStudentStatement(ctx, tx, studentSQL); execErr != nil'. In that error branch change 'pr.Result.Feedback = fmt.Sprintf("SQL Error: %v", execErr)' to 'pr.Result.Feedback = studentSQLErrorFeedback(execErr)', and swap the two recovery statements at :369-:370 so ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT precedes RESET ROLE, matching (2). That branch already ignores both errors and then tx.Rollback()s, so this is a correctness-neutral consistency change; it is specified so both sites read identically and no future reader re-introduces the ordering bug. Leave the :376 post-image capture and the previewRowCap logic untouched.
  BOTH SITES, NOT JUST PREVIEW (answering the explicit question): the graded path at :168 needs this at least as much as preview. Its post-image 'SELECT * FROM <target_table>' is captured into ValidationResult.ValidationDetails, returned to the student on non-dual questions and PERSISTED to app.submissions / practice_attempts, so harvested rows exfiltrate identically; the transaction rollback undoes writes but never undoes READS; and an escaped role inside the graded transaction can additionally read every question's correct_sql/expected_result, grading schema B and every other student's submissions. Privilege escalation inside grading is independently unacceptable regardless of exfiltration.

(4) QUERY PATHS (evaluateQuery :100, evaluateQueryPreview :289) ARE ALREADY SINGLE-STATEMENT-SAFE - DO NOT CHANGE THEM. pgx's Conn.Query (conn.go:751) has NO 'always simple protocol when no arguments' override; it uses config.DefaultQueryExecMode, whose default QueryExecModeCacheStatement goes through Parse/Describe. Measured on the same pool this app builds: tx.Query(ctx, "RESET ROLE; SELECT * FROM bee.secret") returns 'cannot insert multiple commands into a prepared statement (SQLSTATE 42601)'. ONE CHEAP HARDENING IS REQUIRED, because that safety is currently DSN-controlled: pgx honours a 'default_query_exec_mode' runtime param from the connection string (vendored conn.go:192-207), and measured, DATABASE_URL='...?default_query_exec_mode=simple_protocol' makes tx.Query accept 'SELECT 1; SELECT 2' - i.e. a single .env character change would silently reopen this hole on the QUERY path. arch_decisions.req: CRITICAL, LIVE, PREDATES DUAL-SCHEMA: `SET LOCAL ROLE` is not a security boundary in this system at all, because PostgreSQL checks SET ROLE membership against session_user, not current_user, and .env sets DB_USER=postgres so session_user is a SUPERUSER on every evaluation connection. ARCH-021 closed only the semicolon-chained SPELLING of the escape; both live bypasses are SINGLE statements and sail straight through ExecParams. Re-verified by the architect against a live postgres:15-alpine (15.18) in the disposable container claude_impl_todo027_pg, database arch022, NOT the live stack: (a) `BEGIN; SET LOCAL ROLE exam_student_readonly; SET ROLE postgres;` -> SUCCEEDS, current_user becomes postgres, `SELECT * FROM app.system_users` then returns the password-hash row; (b) `BEGIN; SET LOCAL ROLE exam_student_readonly; DO $$ BEGIN RESET ROLE; INSERT INTO sandbox_exam_1.t SELECT pw FROM app.system_users; END $$;` -> ONE statement, and `SELECT * FROM sandbox_exam_1.t` afterwards returned the harvested SECRET_HASH row, which is exactly what the DML post-image capture (postgres_evaluation.go:172) hands back to the student; (c) WORST PATH: evaluateQuery (postgres_evaluation.go:100) and evaluateQueryPreview (:300) use tx.Query(ctx, studentSQL) and never went through ARCH-021 at all, so `DO $$ BEGIN RESET ROLE; EXECUTE 'COPY (SELECT 1) TO PROGRAM ''touch /tmp/pwned_super'''; END $$;` executed and the file WAS created in the container's /tmp and SURVIVED the ROLLBACK (COPY TO PROGRAM is non-transactional) -- i.e. arbitrary shell command execution as the postgres OS user, reachable by any authenticated student answering an ordinary SELECT question. Control, same session, without escalation: `permission denied for schema app` -- so the grant boundary is real and genuinely bypassed. FIX DIRECTION (locked by the user, do not re-derive): execute student SQL on connections whose LOGIN role is itself restricted, so RESET ROLE and SET ROLE land nowhere useful. This closes all four evaluation paths at once and is independent of, and must not be deferred for, scripts/deprivilege_app_db_user.sql.
arch_decisions.decision:
(1) ROLE TOPOLOGY -- FOUR restricted LOGIN roles, one per privilege class; `SET LOCAL ROLE` STAYS.
  The four existing sandbox roles (exam_student, exam_student_readonly, exam_student_preview, exam_student_preview_readonly) and EVERY existing grant site that names them (GrantSchemaPermissions, InitializePracticeSandbox, ResetPracticeSandbox, ensureCategorySchema, ensureExamCurriculumSchema, grantPreviewSchemaPermissions, reconcilePreviewSchemaGrants) are UNCHANGED. Add four new LOGIN roles, each a member of EXACTLY ONE sandbox role:
    quiz_exec_ro        -> member of exam_student_readonly           (graded QUERY; QUERY preview when role==exam_student_readonly)
    quiz_exec_rw        -> member of exam_student                    (graded DML;   DML preview when role==exam_student)
    quiz_exec_prev_ro   -> member of exam_student_preview_readonly   (decoy QUERY preview)
    quiz_exec_prev_rw   -> member of exam_student_preview            (decoy DML preview)
  Attributes at CREATE: LOGIN NOINHERIT NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOREPLICATION NOBYPASSRLS. No GRANTs of their own beyond PostgreSQL's PUBLIC defaults (CONNECT and TEMPORARY on the database, USAGE on schema public).
  WHY SET LOCAL ROLE STAYS (all measured on the disposable PG 15.18): NOINHERIT means the login role by itself holds nothing -- as quiz_exec_ro WITHOUT SET ROLE, `SELECT * FROM public.curriculum` -> `permission denied for table curriculum`; WITH `SET LOCAL ROLE exam_student_readonly` it returns the row. So the pool's idle connections carry zero privilege, every privilege use is explicit and transaction-scoped, and forgetting a SET LOCAL ROLE fails LOUDLY instead of silently running privileged.
  WHY THE MEMBERSHIP DOES NOT RE-OPEN ESCALATION: each login role is a member of exactly one sandbox role, so SET ROLE can only reach the privileges it was already given, and RESET ROLE lands on a zero-privilege role. Measured as quiz_exec_ro: `SET ROLE postgres` -> `permission denied to set role "postgres"`; `SELECT set_config('role','postgres',false)` -> same error; `SET ROLE exam_student` -> `permission denied to set role "exam_student"`; `DO $$ BEGIN RESET ROLE; PERFORM 1 FROM app.system_users; END $$` -> `permission denied for schema app`; and after `DO $$ BEGIN RESET ROLE; END $$` the session's current_user is `quiz_exec_ro`, not postgres.
  WHY FOUR AND NOT ONE (this is the load-bearing part; a single shared login role is WRONG): a login role that is a member of all four was tested (q_login_all) and it MEASURABLY re-opens two boundaries. (i) ARCH-020 REGRESSION: `SET LOCAL ROLE exam_student_preview_readonly; SET ROLE exam_student_readonly;` SUCCEEDED and then read the real curriculum schema in full -- i.e. one shared login role would silently undo ARCH-020. (ii) READ/WRITE CLASS BREAK: `SET LOCAL ROLE exam_student_readonly; DO $$ BEGIN SET ROLE exam_student; INSERT INTO sandbox_exam_1.t VALUES ('poison'); END $$;` SUCCEEDED. Four login roles make both `permission denied to set role`.

(2) CREDENTIAL PROVISIONING -- generated at boot, no new .env secret, no manual DBA step.
  New method on PostgresRepository, in a NEW file /run/media/adamas/large_files/main_project/sql_quiz_system/backend/internal/repository/postgres_student_pool.go: `provisionStudentLoginRoles(ctx) (string, error)`.
  - Generate ONE password shared by all four roles: crypto/rand 32 bytes, hex-encoded (64 chars, [0-9a-f] only). HEX IS DELIBERATE: CREATE/ALTER ROLE cannot take a bind parameter, so the password must be interpolated as a SQL literal; a hex alphabet contains no quote, backslash or dollar sign, so there is nothing to escape and no injection surface. One password for all four is safe because the password is NOT the boundary between classes -- the boundary is WHICH ROLE YOU AUTHENTICATE AS -- and the db service publishes no port (docker-compose.yml has no `ports:` under `db`), so 5432 is reachable only from the compose network. Never log it; never write it to disk.
  - For each of the four roles, run exactly two statements, in this order:
      `DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_catalog.pg_roles WHERE rolname='<role>') THEN CREATE ROLE <role> LOGIN NOINHERIT NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOREPLICATION NOBYPASSRLS; END IF; END $$`
      `ALTER ROLE <role> LOGIN NOINHERIT NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE PASSWORD '<hex>'`
    THE ALTER MUST NOT NAME NOSUPERUSER, NOREPLICATION OR NOBYPASSRLS. Measured: a non-superuser CREATEROLE app role (the posture scripts/deprivilege_app_db_user.sql creates) gets `ERROR: must be superuser to alter superuser roles or change superuser attribute` on `ALTER ROLE ... NOSUPERUSER` and `must be superuser to alter replication roles` on NOREPLICATION, while the exact form above SUCCEEDS. Those attributes are set once at CREATE, which a CREATEROLE role may do. This makes the migration work identically whether the app connects as postgres (today) or as sqlquiz_app (after the deprivilege script).
  - Then `GRANT <sandbox role> TO <login role>` for each of the four pairs (measured to succeed under a CREATEROLE non-superuser too).
  - Idempotent by construction: re-running ALTER simply ROTATES the password on every boot, which is a feature. Existing open sessions are unaffected by a password change.
  - REJECTED: a new .env/compose variable (STUDENT_DB_PASSWORD). It would force the user to edit .env and docker-compose.yml before `docker compose down && up`, it persists a long-lived secret on disk, and it never rotates. Trade-off recorded as OQ-1: the env-var form is the better choice ONLY if the backend is ever run as more than one replica against one database, because two replicas would each rotate the password and invalidate the other's NEW connections (already-open connections survive). Today there is exactly one backend container, so generated-at-boot wins.

(3) POOL LIFECYCLE.
  - `PostgresRepository` gains `studentPools map[string]*pgxpool.Pool` keyed by SANDBOX ROLE NAME ("exam_student", "exam_student_readonly", "exam_student_preview", "exam_student_preview_readonly"), built in /run/media/adamas/large_files/main_project/sql_quiz_system/backend/internal/repository/postgres_student_pool.go.
  - `func (r *PostgresRepository) InitStudentPools(ctx context.Context) error`: calls provisionStudentLoginRoles, then for each class derives a config with `r.pool.Config().Copy()` and overrides ONLY `ConnConfig.User`, `ConnConfig.Password`, `MaxConns`, `MinConns`, `MaxConnIdleTime`. Deriving from the existing pool config is why NO new DSN, host, port, dbname or sslmode setting is needed anywhere. It keeps ARCH-021's `ConnConfig.DefaultQueryExecMode = pgx.QueryExecModeCacheStatement` pin, which MUST be re-asserted defensively after Copy() so the QUERY path on the student pools is extended-protocol too.
  - SIZING (student pools are additive to the existing 20-max privileged pool): exam_student_readonly MaxConns 8; exam_student MaxConns 4 (graded DML is already serialised by the single-worker SubmissionQueue); exam_student_preview 4; exam_student_preview_readonly 4. MinConns 0 for all four (decoy pools are idle in most deployments) and MaxConnIdleTime 5*time.Minute so idle backends are reclaimed. Worst-case total backends 20 + 20 = 40. NOTE FOR OPS (OQ-3): no `max_connections` override exists anywhere in the repo (docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.dev.yml, docker-compose.loadtest.yml, scripts/), so the db container runs the postgres:15-alpine default of 100; 40 fits. The architect deliberately did NOT inspect the live sql-quiz-db container to confirm.
  - BOOT ORDER, /run/media/adamas/large_files/main_project/sql_quiz_system/backend/cmd/main.go: insert `if err := repo.InitStudentPools(ctx); err != nil { log.Fatalf(...) }` IMMEDIATELY AFTER the existing `repo.CreateRestrictedUser(ctx)` call (main.go:57-59) and before InitializeSystemTables. CreateRestrictedUser is what creates the four sandbox roles, so it must run first.
  - FAILURE POLICY: FAIL FAST. Any error provisioning the roles, constructing a pool, or Ping()ing a pool is fatal at boot (log.Fatalf), matching the ID_SALT precedent at main.go:33-35. There is NO degraded mode.
  - `func (r *PostgresRepository) poolForRole(role string) (*pgxpool.Pool, error)` returns the pool for a sandbox role name and returns a non-nil ERROR for an unknown/unprovisioned role. IT MUST NEVER RETURN r.pool. A silent fallback to the privileged pool would restore the exact vulnerability this entry exists to close; make that a comment on the function.
  - `Close()` (postgres.go:149) must close every student pool as well as r.pool.
  - ADVISORY LOCKS: NO CHANGE NEEDED, and this was verified rather than assumed. Advisory-lock keys are database-scoped, not connection- or role-scoped, and require no privilege. Measured: as quiz_exec_ro, `pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared(42)` succeeds; and while a superuser session held `pg_advisory_lock(999)` EXCLUSIVELY, a quiz_exec_ro session got `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock_shared(999)` = FALSE. So acquireSchemaEvalLock on a student pool still interlocks correctly with acquireSchemaRebuildLockTx / ResetPracticeSandbox's session lock on the privileged pool.

(4) WHICH CODE MOVES -- exactly four functions in /run/media/adamas/large_files/main_project/sql_quiz_system/backend/internal/repository/postgres_evaluation.go, and nothing else.
  - evaluateQuery (:58): acquire from poolForRole("exam_student_readonly").
  - evaluateDML (:121): acquire from poolForRole("exam_student").
  - evaluateQueryPreview (:271): acquire from poolForRole(role) using the `role` parameter it is already given.
  - evaluateDMLPreview (:327): acquire from poolForRole(role) using the `role` parameter it is already given.
  In each, ONLY the `r.pool.Acquire(ctx)` line changes; the ENTIRE remaining transaction stays on that one connection and is otherwise untouched -- acquireSchemaEvalLock, SAVEPOINT student_eval, SET LOCAL search_path, SET LOCAL ROLE, execStudentStatement / tx.Query(studentSQL), the post-image `SELECT * FROM <target_table>`, collectRowsWithColumns, ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT, RESET ROLE and Commit. All of these were measured to work verbatim as a restricted non-superuser: a full rehearsal of the evaluateDML shape (advisory lock -> savepoint -> SET LOCAL search_path -> SET LOCAL ROLE exam_student -> INSERT -> post-image SELECT -> ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT -> RESET ROLE -> COMMIT) ran green end to end as quiz_exec_rw's stand-in. A poolForRole error must be returned as a Go error from the evaluate function (boot already guarantees it cannot happen).
  - NONE of these four functions reads app.* or any privileged object -- confirmed by reading all four in full -- so nothing else has to move with them.
  - EXPLICITLY DOES NOT MOVE, stays on the privileged r.pool: the LECTURER ANSWER-CAPTURE PATH (CreateQuestion / Phase-0 capture in postgres_questions.go, captureExpectedResult in postgres_practice.go), PreviewCorrectSQL / PreviewCorrectSQLInSchema, every schema import, every GRANT/DDL/EnsureSchema, ResolveTargetTable, reconcilePreviewSchemaGrants, ResetPracticeSandbox, and everything in postgres_core.go / postgres_users.go / postgres_exams.go / postgres_results.go / postgres_export.go / postgres_images.go. Those execute LECTURER SQL or app SQL and legitimately need the app role.

(5) plpgsql -- YES, REVOKE, WITH A MANDATORY PAIRED GRANT. Supplementary only, exactly as the brief says.
  Add to CreateRestrictedUser's statement list, IN THIS ORDER AND BEFORE any other statement in that function (the ordering is load-bearing, see below):
      `GRANT USAGE ON LANGUAGE plpgsql TO CURRENT_USER`
      `REVOKE USAGE ON LANGUAGE plpgsql FROM PUBLIC`
      `REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION pg_catalog.pg_terminate_backend(integer, bigint) FROM PUBLIC`
      `REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION pg_catalog.pg_cancel_backend(integer) FROM PUBLIC`
  MEASURED CONSEQUENCES: after the revoke, `DO $$ ... $$` as a student -> `permission denied for language plpgsql`; `CREATE FUNCTION ... LANGUAGE plpgsql` as a student -> same; an ALREADY-EXISTING plpgsql TRIGGER in a lecturer-imported schema STILL FIRES for the student (executing a plpgsql function needs EXECUTE on the function, not USAGE on the language), so lecturer imports that define trigger functions keep working; bare `SET ROLE` is COMPLETELY UNAFFECTED, confirming this is supplementary and not a substitute for (1); `CREATE FUNCTION ... LANGUAGE sql` is still allowed to students, which is accepted because a SQL-language body cannot issue SET ROLE or any other utility command.
  LEGITIMATE plpgsql USE IN THIS CODEBASE: the APP'S OWN boot migrations use anonymous DO blocks (postgres_schema.go CreateRestrictedUser :33-:50, migrateQuestionsIdentity :151-:166, and the new role provisioning in (2)). company_elmasri_postgres.sql contains none. THE FOOTGUN, MEASURED: with plpgsql revoked from PUBLIC, a non-superuser CREATEROLE app role FAILED its own `DO $$ ... $$` migration with `permission denied for language plpgsql`, and succeeded again only after `GRANT USAGE ON LANGUAGE plpgsql TO <app role>`. Today DB_USER=postgres bypasses the revoke as superuser (verified: a DO block still ran fine as postgres after the revoke), so nothing breaks now -- but WITHOUT the paired GRANT this would brick the backend's boot the moment scripts/deprivilege_app_db_user.sql is applied. `GRANT USAGE ON LANGUAGE plpgsql TO CURRENT_USER` was verified to be valid PG15 syntax and makes the migration self-healing under either app role. It must be the FIRST statement in the list so that a boot which is re-running after a partial previous boot can still execute the DO blocks that follow.
  The pg_terminate_backend/pg_cancel_backend revokes address a MEASURED residual (see (6.1)); the app calls neither function anywhere.

(6) RESIDUALS ONCE THE LOGIN ROLE IS NON-SUPERUSER -- what is closed, and what is honestly still open.
  CLOSED (each measured as quiz_exec_ro's stand-in, after SET LOCAL ROLE and again after an in-DO RESET ROLE):
    - `COPY (SELECT 1) TO PROGRAM 'touch /tmp/...'` -> `must be superuser or have privileges of the pg_execute_server_program role`; NO file appeared in the container. This is the headline RCE from the req, gone.
    - `COPY (SELECT 1) TO '/tmp/...'` -> `must be superuser or have privileges of the pg_write_server_files role`; no file.
    - `pg_read_file` / `lo_import` / `lo_export` -> `permission denied for function ...`. So pg_read_server_files, pg_write_server_files, pg_execute_server_program and the large-object server-side file functions need NO extra REVOKE: PostgreSQL already gates them on superuser-or-explicit-role-membership, and the four login roles are members of nothing but their one sandbox role.
    - `SET ROLE postgres`, `SELECT set_config('role','postgres',false)`, `SET ROLE <another sandbox role>` -> `permission denied to set role`.
    - `CREATE TABLE public.x` -> `permission denied for schema public` (PG15 already removed PUBLIC's CREATE on schema public).
    - `DO $$ BEGIN ...; COMMIT; END $$` inside the evaluation's explicit transaction -> `invalid transaction termination`, so the always-rollback contract of every evaluation path cannot be escaped from inside student SQL.
  STILL OPEN, ENUMERATED DELIBERATELY:
    6.1 SAME-ROLE BACKEND SIGNALLING. Measured BEFORE mitigation: a quiz_exec_rw session successfully ran `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE usename='q_login_rw'` and killed another live session of the same login role -- a student could kill other students' in-flight evaluations of the same class. Mitigated by the two REVOKEs in (5); measured AFTER: `permission denied for function pg_terminate_backend`. Cross-class signalling was never possible because the four classes use four different login roles.
    6.2 CREATE TEMP TABLE remains available (TEMPORARY on the database is granted to PUBLIC by default). It does NOT persist onto a pooled connection -- measured: after ROLLBACK, zero relations remain in any pg_temp schema -- because every evaluation path rolls the student's DDL back. arch_decisions.rationale: Restricting the LOGIN role is the only mechanism that is enforced by PostgreSQL's own privilege system rather than by anything the application spells correctly, so it is immune to whichever statement shape the next bypass uses -- SET ROLE, RESET ROLE, set_config('role',...), a DO block, or something not yet thought of. arch_decisions.req: FEATURE 2 (backend). arch_decisions.decision:
(1) ONE ENDPOINT WITH A MODE DISCRIMINATOR, not three. POST /api/v1/users/bulk-reset-password, registered in the existing admin-only group in /run/media/adamas/large_files/main_project/sql_quiz_system/backend/cmd/main.go (`adminUsers`, :200-210, already behind RoleMiddleware(models.RoleAdmin)). A static sibling of /:id routes is safe here - the same group already mixes `adminUsers.GET("/all")` with `adminUsers.PUT("/:id")`. WHY ONE: the three modes differ ONLY in how the target set is resolved; everything after resolution (generate, hash, persist, bump, log, project into the response) is identical, so three endpoints would triplicate the security-critical half. The mode is an explicit enum, never inferred from which optional field happens to be present.

(2) REQUEST (all fields validated before ANY write):
    {
      "mode": "ids" | "all_students" | "exam_roster",
      "user_ids": ["<opaque user token>", ...],   // required and non-empty iff mode=="ids"; max 1000
      "exam_id": "<opaque exam token>",            // required iff mode=="exam_roster"
      "confirm": "RESET",                          // REQUIRED literal on EVERY request, including continuation batches
      "after_user_id": "<opaque user token>",      // optional continuation cursor; absent = start
      "batch_size": 100                            // optional; default 100, hard max 200
    }
  Validation order, all pre-write: confirm != "RESET" -> 400 {"error":"confirmation_required"}; unknown mode -> 400; mode/field mismatch -> 400; batch_size clamped to [1,200]; len(user_ids) > 1000 -> 400 {"error":"too_many_ids"}.

(3) TARGET RESOLUTION - new repository file /run/media/adamas/large_files/main_project/sql_quiz_system/backend/internal/repository/postgres_password_bulk.go (a NEW file so postgres_users.go stays untouched and file-disjoint):
    func (r *PostgresRepository) ResolveBulkResetTargets(ctx context.Context, mode string, userIDs []int, examID int, afterID int, limit int) (targets []models.BulkResetTarget, remaining int, err error)
  All three modes select the SAME columns (id, username, COALESCE(student_number,''), COALESCE(first_name,''), COALESCE(last_name,''), COALESCE(sec_lec,''), COALESCE(sec_lab,'')) from app.system_users, with `role = 'STUDENT'`, `id > $afterID`, `ORDER BY id ASC`, `LIMIT $limit`, plus a second COUNT query with the same predicates minus LIMIT for `remaining`. mode filters: all_students adds nothing; exam_roster adds `JOIN app.exam_students es ON es.student_id = u.id AND es.exam_id = $examID`; ids adds `AND u.id = ANY($userIDs)`.
    func (r *PostgresRepository) NonStudentUserIDs(ctx context.Context, userIDs []int) ([]int, error)
  For mode=="ids" ONLY: returns every supplied id that does not exist or whose role != 'STUDENT'. arch_decisions.req: FEATURE 2 (security). The bulk endpoint returns many plaintext passwords in one response and the frontend writes them to a downloadable CSV - a roster-wide credential dump. Record the controls as BINDING constraints for implementors, and rule on whether CSV/print generation must be client-side.
arch_decisions.decision:
THESE ARE CONSTRAINTS, NOT SUGGESTIONS. A TODO that ships without any one of them must be failed by the validator.

  S1 ADMIN ROLE ONLY. The route is registered inside the `adminUsers` group (cmd/main.go:200-210), which already applies RoleMiddleware(models.RoleAdmin) on top of AuthMiddleware. It must NOT be added to the `staff` group or given a Lecturer role. Lecturers can already see rosters; they must not be able to mint credentials for a whole class.
  S2 STUDENT-ONLY TARGETS. Enforced server-side (ARCH-031 (3)). No mode can ever resolve an ADMIN or LECTURER row, and mode=ids rejects the whole request if one is named. The actor cannot reset themselves through this path.
  S3 EXPLICIT CONFIRMATION ON THE WIRE. Every request - including continuation batches - must carry "confirm":"RESET" verbatim, or the server refuses with 400 before any write. The UI additionally requires the admin to type the phrase; the server does not trust the UI for this.
  S4 NO EMAIL DELIVERY OF ANY KIND on this path: no SendCredential to students, and no SendChangeNotice to ADMIN_EMAIL. Concretely: BulkResetPasswords must not reference s.email and must not call s.logPasswordEvent.
  S5 NO PLAINTEXT IN SERVER LOGS OR SERVER STORAGE. Passwords, bcrypt hashes and password_events ciphertext never appear in any log line. No file, no temp dir, no cache, no session, no in-memory 'last batch' is retained after the response is written. There is no endpoint that can re-fetch a generated plaintext; the ONLY way to recover one afterwards is the existing per-user GET /users/:id/password-events, which is admin-only and requires PASSWORD_LOG_KEY.
  S6 STRUCTURED AUDIT OF ACTOR AND AFFECTED SET. Exactly one log line per request: actor username + internal id, mode, exam_id (0 when N/A), requested/succeeded/failed counts, and the internal ids of the affected set. Plus the durable per-student `admin_reset` rows in app.password_events (when a key is configured), which already record changed_by.
  S7 RESPONSE HYGIENE. `Cache-Control: no-store` on the response. The endpoint is POST only (never GET), so credentials can never land in a URL, a browser history entry, a proxy access log or a Referer header.
  S8 SESSION INVALIDATION IS PART OF THE OPERATION, not an optional extra: token_version is bumped inside the same per-student transaction as the password write (ARCH-031 (3)), so a reset student's existing JWTs die immediately.
  S9 BOUNDED BLAST RADIUS PER REQUEST: <=200 students per call, <=1000 ids in one request body.

CLIENT-SIDE GENERATION: CONFIRMED, not overruled. The CSV, the printable table and the slips MUST be produced in the browser from the response body, reusing the existing /run/media/adamas/large_files/main_project/sql_quiz_system/frontend/src/utils/csv.ts (toCsv/downloadCsv, already unit-tested in src/__tests__/utils/csv.test.ts). Reasons: (i) a server-generated file would have to be stored or re-served, which creates exactly the re-fetchable plaintext artifact this design is trying not to have; (ii) a download endpoint cannot carry the Authorization header from a plain link - this repo already hit that bug and documented it at the top of csv.ts ('avoiding token-in-URL downloads ... which previously 401'd the /export-scores endpoint'), and the workaround for a credential dump would be a token in a URL; (iii) client-side keeps the plaintext's lifetime equal to the tab's lifetime. Corollary constraints for the frontend: NEVER write results to localStorage / sessionStorage / IndexedDB / a Pinia-style persisted store; keep them in component state only; register a beforeunload guard while unsaved results are held; provide an explicit 'Clear results' control that drops them from memory.

ACCEPTED RESIDUALS, recorded rather than hidden: (a) there is no rate limiting anywhere in this codebase, so a compromised admin session can call this repeatedly - the audit log is the only detective control; (b) the printed slips are physical paper and their handling is a process problem, not a software one; (c) an admin who prints and does not distribute has effectively locked those students out until they distribute - the UI must say so before the admin confirms.
arch_decisions.rationale: The dangerous property of this feature is not any single line of code, it is that one click turns into hundreds of live credentials in one HTTP body. So the controls that matter are the ones that bound WHO can do it, WHICH accounts it can touch, HOW MANY at a time, whether it can happen by accident, and whether the plaintext can be recovered later by anyone who did not see the original response. Confirming client-side generation is not a stylistic preference: the alternative forces a server-side artifact plus an authenticated download path, and this repo has already been bitten by exactly that shape. Writing the controls down as numbered constraints gives the todo-creator one TODO per control and the validator a literal checklist.
